relations.statement: There exists u : Code such that for all codes c and n, eval u (Nat.pair (encode c) n) = eval c n
univCode.eval [x] = pure <$> univFun x for all x

lemmas.statement: exists u : Code, forall c n, eval u (pair (encode c) n) = eval c n
lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem L1 : ∃ u : Nat.Partrec.Code, ∀ (c : Nat.Partrec.Code) (n : ℕ), Nat.Partrec.Code.eval u (Nat.pair (Encodable.encode c) n) = Nat.Partrec.Code.eval c n := GenesisComputation.Universal.universal_code

lemmas.statement: exists a ToPartrec code cu with cu.eval [x] = pure <$> univFun x for all x
lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem L2 : ∃ cu : Turing.ToPartrec.Code, ∀ x : ℕ, cu.eval [x] = pure <$> GenesisComputation.Universal.univFun x := GenesisComputation.Universal.univCode_exists

near_misses.rejecting_invariant: eval c n may diverge, and univFun is only partial recursive (Partrec), not total

open_obligations: Link between the Nat.Partrec.Code u from universal_code and univFun is not cited explicitly; needs a bridging lemma that univFun x = eval u x
Statement of the conjunction (the same function on a single natural number via ToPartrec) is not packaged as one theorem
Lemma Lean skeletons are not elaborated by me, so claims_proved is false
